Header: Erwinia tracheiphila In Sinhala: Bacteria melaweema

Prevention: If previous crop was a cucurbit, plough the field during the dry period to expose and destroy larval and pupal stages
Remove volunteer and wild cucurbit plants in and around fields
Proper weed control since bacteria can survive on some weeds without showing symptoms
PMDG for further details on management
Monitoring: Reported to be transmitted by cucumber beetles.
Then it needs continuous monitoring of the cucumber beetles in the field
Disease is most serious on bitter gourd, cucumber and snake gourd
Observe for disease symptoms: longitudinal splits on tender green stems
Brown to grey water soaked lesions on mature stems
Sporadic wilting of plants first appearing on a branch
Under wet climatic conditions, cream coloured bacterial ooze droplets are seen on infected lesions
Drying off and death of whole plants
Direct Control: Disease may be reduced by controlling the cucumber beetles by applying neem oil at a rate of 2ml per litre of water
EC ( 30ml/10l; 960-2400 ml /ha based on the stage of the crop) to control vector (Tentative recommendation)
Restrictions: Restrictions if severe infestation of cucumber beetle occurs, spray recommended insecticides
Avoid drinking, eating and smoking during the spray
Use safety measures i.e. gloves, cloths, gum boots, masks and goggles while handling and spraying the pesticides
II (Moderately hazardous); Mature plants are less vulnerable to severe damage; Insecticides are under testing, Profenophos has identified as a promising one
